patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in crm, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Both sit in crm, but documented company-size audiences diverge. Choose Mailchimp only if your buying job matches “Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing).” rather than Pega CRM's shape. Choose Pega CRM only if your buying job matches “Pega enterprise CRM; custom quote only.” rather than Mailchimp's shape. Workflow advantage: Mailchimp leans lead-management, inbound-sales; Pega CRM leans sales-automation, pipeline-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in crm, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Mailchimp is Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing).; Pega CRM is Pega enterprise CRM; custom quote only..
- Company-size focus: Mailchimp (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Pega CRM (enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Mailchimp-leaning lead-management, inbound-sales vs Pega CRM-leaning sales-automation, pipeline-management, complex-sales-processes.
- Researched limits: Mailchimp — Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform; Pega CRM — Enterprise custom quote — no SMB list pricing.

Limitations — Mailchimp: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform; Paid pricing is contact-based and changes — verify live; Pega CRM: Enterprise custom quote — no SMB list pricing; High implementation and admin overhead.

Poor-fit cases: Mailchimp is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform · Pega CRM is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Enterprise custom quote — no SMB list pricing · Avoid Mailchimp if you actually need Pega CRM's motion (Pega enterprise CRM; custom quote only.)
